title: Time (minutes and seconds)
status: draft: written 13 Nov 2026 from research round 3; shorter entries; not yet checked by a Kenyan maths teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Time is the one measure that does not regroup at ten, a hundred or a thousand, and calculations with time are among the weakest items in national tests elsewhere (source 72). Every calculation here should name the 60 aloud ('sixty seconds make a minute') and use the clock face, where one full turn of the second hand is the picture of 60.

skills.key_step: The child picks out the second hand as the thin hand that moves fastest (and the seconds digits on a digital display) and names the second as what it measures.

floor.prerequisite: Reads hours and minutes on a clock (Grade 4).
floor.question: Which hand shows the hour?

representations: a real or drawn clock with three hands
steps: Watch the hands: which moves fastest?
Name it the second hand; it ticks once a second.
Find the seconds on a digital clock (the last pair).

board.do: Draw a clock with three hands; animate the thin hand ticking.
Ask which hand moved before naming it.
Wait for the child to point it out.

misconceptions.ask: Watch for ten ticks. Which long hand moved a lot?
misconceptions.repair: The thin fast hand is seconds; the thicker long hand creeps one mark each minute.

checks.question: On a clock, how do you know which hand is the second hand?
checks.answer: It is thin and moves fastest, ticking every second

checks.question: A digital clock shows 10:24:37. Which digits are the seconds?

skills.key_step: The child judges about how long a second, ten seconds and a minute feel by timing real actions.

floor.question: Clap once. About how long did that take?

representations: a list of actions with times
steps: Time actions: 10 claps, writing your name, running across the field.
Match actions to about 1 s, 10 s, 1 minute.

board.do: Write three headings: about 1 second, about 10 seconds, about 1 minute.
Child sorts: one clap, writing your name, singing the national anthem's first verse, tying a shoe.
Wait for the child to explain one choice.

misconceptions.ask: Count to ten while I watch the second hand. Did it go round as far as you counted?
misconceptions.repair: Count with a steady word between numbers and check against the clock.

checks.question: Which takes about 10 seconds: blinking, writing your full name, or walking to the next town?
About how long does it take to tie a shoe: 1 second, 10 seconds or 10 minutes?

skills.key_step: The child counts in fives from 12 to the numeral before the second hand, then adds the small marks.
representations: the face with fives written outside
steps: Count in fives from 12 to the numeral before the hand.
Add the small marks past it.
Read the full time: hours, minutes, seconds.
contexts: timing a race on the school clock

board.do: Draw a clock; second hand two small marks past the 4.
Child counts in fives from 12 to the 4 as the board writes each five outside.
Wait for the child to add the small marks.

misconceptions.ask: How many small marks from 12 to 4?
misconceptions.repair: Each numeral is five marks further: count the fives.

misconceptions.ask: What is the 4 worth in seconds before you add the marks?
misconceptions.repair: Change the numeral to its five-times value first (20), then add the marks.

checks.question: The second hand points exactly at the 4. How many seconds?
The second hand is two small marks past the 7. How many seconds?

skills.key_step: The child names each pair on a digital display (hh:mm:ss, or mm:ss on a stopwatch) before reading it.

floor.prerequisite: Reads hh:mm on a digital clock.
floor.question: Read 08:15.

representations: the display with each pair labelled
steps: Label the pairs: hours, minutes, seconds.
A stopwatch has only minutes and seconds.
contexts: a phone stopwatch at sports day

board.do: Write 02:35 as a stopwatch display.
Point at each pair.
board.say: What does this pair count on a stopwatch?

board.do: Wait for the child to label and read it.

misconceptions.ask: Did Achieng run round the field for two hours?
misconceptions.repair: A stopwatch starts at minutes and seconds; check if the time is sensible.

misconceptions.ask: There are three pairs. What does the last one count?
misconceptions.repair: Label all three pairs before reading.

checks.question: A stopwatch shows 02:35 after a run round the field. How long?
A clock shows 08:15:42. Write the time in words.

skills.key_step: The child says 60 seconds make 1 minute and explains with the clock: one full turn of the second hand while the minute hand moves one mark.

floor.question: Count in fives from 12 all the way round.

representations: one full turn of the second hand
steps: Watch the second hand go once round; count in fives.
Notice the minute hand moved one mark.

board.do: Animate the second hand going once round slowly, writing fives outside as it passes each numeral.
Child counts in fives to the end.
Point at the minute hand, which has moved one mark.
board.say: What did the minute hand do?

board.do: Wait for the child to say the relationship.

misconceptions.ask: Count the fives all the way round the clock. Where do you stop?
misconceptions.repair: Time is the measure that changes at 60, not 100. The clock face shows it.

misconceptions.ask: How many small marks between 12 and 1?
misconceptions.repair: Each numeral is five seconds apart: 12 numerals, 60 seconds.

checks.question: How many seconds in 1 minute?
The second hand goes from 12 all the way round to 12. How long?

skills.key_step: The child multiplies minutes by 60 and adds the extra seconds.

board.do: Draw four full clock turns and a quarter-ish extra labelled 15 s.
Child counts in sixties along the turns.
Wait for the child to add the 15 seconds.

misconceptions.ask: How many seconds in one minute?
misconceptions.repair: Count in sixties, not hundreds.

misconceptions.ask: Is 415 seconds about four minutes?
misconceptions.repair: Change the minutes first (240 s), then add the 15.

checks.question: A song lasts 3 minutes. How many seconds?
Kamau boiled water in 4 min 15 s. How many seconds?

skills.key_step: The child groups seconds in sixties (or divides by 60) and gives the answer as minutes and leftover seconds.
contexts: a matatu waiting at the stage

board.do: Write 150 s.
Child takes off 60 and 60, writing a minute each time.
Wait for the child to say what is left.

misconceptions.ask: Is 100 seconds one minute?
misconceptions.repair: Take away 60s, not 100s.

misconceptions.ask: Half a minute is how many seconds?
misconceptions.repair: Use the leftover seconds, not the decimal digits.

misconceptions.ask: A minute is longer than a second. More minutes or fewer?
misconceptions.repair: Bigger unit, fewer of them: take away sixties (divide by 60).

checks.question: A matatu waited 150 seconds. Write this in minutes and seconds.
Convert 120 seconds to minutes.

skills.key_step: The child adds seconds and minutes in columns, regrouping every 60 seconds as 1 minute and adding the carried minute.

floor.prerequisite: Converts seconds to minutes and seconds.
floor.question: 75 s = ___ min ___ s

steps: Add the seconds; 60 or more makes a minute.
Add the minutes with the carry.
contexts: sweeping the classroom and the verandah

board.do: Write 3 min 45 s + 2 min 30 s in columns.
Point at the seconds column.
board.say: Add the seconds. Is it 60 or more?

board.do: Wait for 75 s and the regrouping.
Child carries the minute and finishes.

misconceptions.ask: Is 75 seconds more than a minute?
misconceptions.repair: Sixty seconds become a minute; carry it.

misconceptions.ask: When does a minute fill up: at 60 seconds or 100?
misconceptions.repair: Picture the second hand going round once: 60.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the minute from the 75 seconds go?
misconceptions.repair: Write the carried minute above the minutes column and add it.

checks.question: 2 min 50 s + 1 min 40 s
Njeri swept for 3 min 45 s and then 2 min 30 s. Total?

skills.key_step: The child exchanges 1 minute for 60 seconds when there are too few seconds, and reduces the minutes by one.
steps: Exchange 1 min for 60 s if needed.
contexts: how much longer a bus took

board.do: Write 5 min 20 s - 2 min 45 s in columns.
Point at 20 above 45.
Wait for the child to exchange a minute.

misconceptions.ask: How many seconds does one minute give you?
misconceptions.repair: One minute is 60 seconds: 20 + 60 = 80.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the extra 60 seconds come from?
misconceptions.repair: Cross out the minute you exchanged.

misconceptions.ask: Add your answer to 2 min 45 s. Do you get 5 min 20 s?
misconceptions.repair: The check fails; exchange 1 minute for 60 seconds.

checks.question: Wanjiru ran in 5 min 20 s and Otieno in 2 min 45 s. How much longer did Wanjiru take?
6 min 10 s - 1 min 50 s

skills.key_step: The child multiplies both minutes and seconds and regroups every 60 seconds of the product as 1 minute.

board.do: Draw 3 pans, each labelled 2 min 25 s.
Ask for an estimate in minutes.
Child multiplies the seconds and regroups.

misconceptions.ask: Does each batch take 25 seconds as well?
misconceptions.repair: Both parts happen three times.

misconceptions.ask: 120 seconds is how many minutes?
misconceptions.repair: Take away 60s: 120 s is 2 minutes exactly.

misconceptions.ask: Is 75 seconds more than a minute?
misconceptions.repair: Regroup 60 seconds as a minute.

checks.question: One batch of mandazi takes 2 min 25 s. How long do 3 batches take?
2 min 40 s x 3

skills.key_step: The child divides the minutes, changes any leftover minute into 60 seconds, adds it to the seconds, then divides.
steps: Divide minutes; carry the leftover as 60 s.

board.do: Write 7 min 30 s ÷ 2 with a box for the leftover minute.
Wait for the child to say what the leftover minute becomes.
Child adds 60 to the seconds and divides.

misconceptions.ask: Each pupil got 3 minutes. Is a minute left over?
misconceptions.repair: Share the leftover minute as 60 seconds.

misconceptions.ask: How many seconds is the leftover minute?
Did each lap take all 40 seconds?
misconceptions.repair: Both parts are shared; check by multiplying back.

checks.question: Mwalimu shares 7 min 30 s of reading time equally between 2 pupils. How long each?
A runner does 2 laps in 6 min 40 s at a steady pace. How long per lap?
